provenance.construction: Reproduction of the two-yoked-surface chain code check matrix q40_24_4.txt of Hirai and Suzuki (arXiv:2610.04613 Sec. IV.1-IV.3), taken from github.com/yugahirai/multi_yoked_surface_codes @ b3e8b3e, `ecc/chain_codes/2_yoke/q40_24_4.txt`, used verbatim: the published max check weight already sits at the board cap, so nothing was changed. Re-derived here and re-verified (CSS commutation, k, and the distance witness) rather than copied from the paper's table.
provenance.notes: Reproduction of the published matrix, not a new construction: the checks come from github.com/yugahirai/multi_yoked_surface_codes @ b3e8b3e, `ecc/chain_codes/2_yoke/q40_24_4.txt`, unchanged for the two-yoke entries and re-generated as an equivalent basis of the same row space for the three-yoke ones. Checked against the current board by exact fingerprint and WL signature with local-Hadamard images included: exact_duplicate_of=None, wl_equivalent_of=None, board_advancing=True, dominated_by=[]. qldpc submit runs its own dedup pass after writing this file, so the draft body first matched the candidate against itself; the verdict above was taken with the file off the board. Literature novelty: known_parameters -- the parameter set is published in arXiv:2610.04613.

circuit.notes: Generic sequential two-block extraction: one ancilla per check, X checks then Z checks each round with joint reset and measurement layers; CX layers are a proper edge coloring of each Tanner graph (16 X + 16 Z CX layers per round, coloring candidate 1); generated by qldpc submit (research/circuit_autogen.py, seed 0), the first of up to 6 candidates whose RIS screen at 2 rounds found nothing below d; witnesses from RIS on ker(H_dem) at twice the gate's trial budget, validated in GF(2)

contributed_by.method: Simulated annealing over site assignments on an integer grid with the repo's own research/local2d/fold_layout.search_layout (max-diameter objective, several bounding boxes and seeds); single layer at radius 4 tried first, then two layers at 7. Radius and per-site occupancy re-measured with the verifier's rule.
